preconditioning.notes: Estimated: no page for the Ioniq Electric describes a battery warming or conditioning feature (Hyundai UK press kit and US 2020 release do not mention one), and Hyundai Motor Group presents navigation-triggered battery conditioning as new with the 2022-2023 IONIQ 5, years after this car. Caveat: Canadian Ioniq Electrics may have had a battery heater (the Kona Electric did); not checked.

chemistry.notes: EVSpecifications.com 2020 Ioniq Electric 38.3 kWh: battery type "NCM622" (LiNiCoMnO2). Community database, not a Hyundai statement.

ac_max_kw.notes: Hyundai US 2020 release: 7.2 kW onboard charger (up from 6.6). Canadian figure assumed the same.

dc_max_kw.notes: InsideEVs: peak fell to "just under 50 kW" (about 40-45 kW to 50 %, Fastned data), recorded as 50; Fastned lists 45 kW; Wikipedia says the car accepts only a 50 kW fast charge. Hyundai's 54 min to 80 % is on a 100 kW station.
